overall_summary: Cosmic anomalies and extreme planetary weather are the primary growth drivers for FACTVERSE, with 'The Planet of Burning Ice' leading at over 1,000 views. Conversely, cognitive psychology and brain-related facts struggle to gain traction, typically stalling under 100 views. Shorter, high-impact sensory hooks (smells, tastes, extreme temperatures) in space themes yield the highest retention and engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Cosmic Anomalies & Sensory Space Facts
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,053 views), 'The Largest Ocean in Space' (460 views), 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views), and 'The Planet Where It Rains Molten Iron!' (329 views) are the top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space-themed videos focusing on extreme physics, bizarre planetary weather, and cosmic sensory comparisons (smell, taste, sound).

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views), 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views), and 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (52 views) consistently underperform.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from internal cognitive psychology and brain mechanics unless framed through a highly dramatic, external sci-fi or historical lens.

next_video.concept: The Planet Where It Rains Liquid Rubies and Sapphires
next_video.opening_direction: There is a giant planet in deep space where it literally rains precious gemstones...
next_video.twist_direction: ...but the winds are so violent, these liquid rubies fly sideways at 5,000 miles per hour, shredding anything in their path.
next_video.reason: Space anomalies with extreme weather and high-value visual hooks (gems, rain, extreme speed) perfectly match the profile of our top-performing Shorts.

experiment: Test a 14-second Short on a historical space mystery (e.g., the 1977 Wow! Signal or a lost astronaut transmission) to see if combining historical storytelling with cosmic themes can replicate the high engagement of planetary facts.
